title: DHS proposes new $100K filing fee on H-1B visa petitions
content: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on Monday published a proposal for a $103, 265 fee imposed on those filing a cap-subject petition for an H-1B visa. The new fee would apply to all H-1B petitions, regardless of if the worker is inside or outside of the US, except for those filed by universities, certain non-profits like hospitals, government positions, or visa renewals. This proposal follows the June declaration by a federal judge and a subsequent affirmation by an appeals court, that US President Trump’s previous $100,000 fee on H-1B visas violated the separation of powers doctrine and was therefore unconstitutional. As attempts to implement the original fee proved unsuccessful, at least temporarily, the Trump administration has taken a different avenue to further this piece of their agenda, using agency rule-making as opposed to presidential power . The H-1B visa program is the most common way for employers to retain temporary foreign workers in speciality positions. Visas issued under the program by US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) are capped at 65,o00 per fiscal year and the proposed fee applies to any visa petition that is not exempt from the cap. Additionally, the fee is applied on top of all other fees incurred in applying for the visa, including the previous, and potentially revivable, 100,000 fee, and it is only an application fee, not a guarantee that the visa will be approved. H-1B workers make up approximately 730,000 employees in the US and contribute an estimated $86 billion to the federal economy and $11 billion to state and local tax revenues. DHS indicated in their rule that the purpose of the fee is to recover immigration and customs related costs incurred by federal agencies in enforcing mechanisms of “the lawful immigration system.” Acquired funds will be put towards operations like immigration court proceedings, consular visa processing, enforcing labor standards, and inspection and enforcement activities
author: Abigail Austin | Vermont Law & Graduate School, US

title: Amnesty International calls for children to be included in youth digital rights regulatory processes
content: Amnesty International reported on Monday that international failure to ensure children’s online safety from Big Tech harms is connected to a lack of the youth perspective in policymaking spaces. Classifying existing solutions as performative, the organization points out that increasing surveillance, data tracking, and censorship is a major threat to their safety. Children face “r isks such as cyberbullying, grooming, online violence, and problematic social media use” while their data is “constantly collected, tracked and shared” by “a largely invisible network of government and private actors, in most cases without free and informed consent.” In a recent brief , the UN attributed these issues to technology companies that are financially incentivized to maximize revenue. These companies profit from tailoring content to users’ emotional vulnerabilities and related habits. Children are uniquely susceptible to these activities. Specifically, “algorithmic and AI systems can keep young users hooked, trapping them in harmful, never ending content loops and exposing them to increasingly extreme material, including self-harm and suicide content, pornography, extremism and violence.” Furthermore, data is tracked outside of social media in schools and universities, which collect biometric attendance data and leverage AI-enabled performance metrics. Many countries have addressed social media concerns by instituting bans for underaged children. Turkey requires platforms to establish age-verification systems and restrict age-inappropriate content access. Australia declared Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, Twitch, X, YouTube, Kick and Reddit to be age-restricted platforms inaccessible to children under the age of sixteen. Other countries that have enacted similar bans include Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Various countries are strongly considering such a ban, including Britain, Denmark, Greec

title: US Supreme Court lifts block on Trump mail voting executive order
content: The US Supreme Court stayed a district court injunction Monday that had blocked President Donald Trump’s executive order overhauling mail voting, ruling in a per curiam opinion that the states had not shown an injury concrete and imminent enough to make their claims justiciable before the November midterm election. In Trump v. California , No. 26A124 (a related application in Alabama v. California , No. 26A139, was denied as moot), the court found the government likely to succeed on its argument that the states’ claims are not justiciable, because it considered the order itself, in its words, “an internal directive from the President to his subordinates” that “neither requires nor forbids anything of anyone outside the Executive Branch.” Justice Sonia Sotomayor, joined by Justice Elena Kagan, and Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson each dissented separately. Executive Order No. 14399 , issued in March, directs the US Department of Homeland Security to compile state-by-state “Citizenship List[s]” of voters, instructs the US Department of Justice to prioritize prosecuting officials who issue ballots to ineligible voters, and directs the US Postal Service to initiate a proposed rulemaking on mail ballot envelopes, including a barcode requirement. The court measured the states’ injury when they sued, before the Postal Service had proposed any rule, and found the harm too speculative to support standing. The Homeland Security Secretary may compile the lists only “to the extent feasible and consistent with applicable law,” and prosecutions are limited to conduct “consistent with applicable law.” Since then, the Postal Service has proposed the rule and finalized it , effective August 21, three days before Monday’s ruling. A coalition of 23 states and the District of Columbia sued in the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, where Judge Indira Talwani entered a final judgment barrin
author: Leah Talyansky | Vermont Law & Graduate School, US

title: New Zealand PM introduces under-16 social media and AI companion ban
content: The New Zealand government announced on Monday that it had introduced a bill to ban social media for children under 16. The law would require social media platforms and social AI companions to verify users’ ages before providing services. The Online Safety (Minimum Age and Child Safety Risk Assessment) Bill would require an age restriction on platforms with harmful features for children. These features include recommender systems, endless feeds, feedback features and time-limited features. The bill also seeks to restrict underage users from accessing AI companion services. However, it explicitly excludes messaging apps, professional networking sites, gaming and music platforms, and other educational and health tools. Notably, age verification through self-declared dates of birth and formal identification does not satisfy the platforms’ duty under the law. It also requires platforms to verify their users’ age through other methods such as facial scans and user activity patterns. The bill would also require platforms to conduct child safety risk assessments for all users under 18 and protect them from harmful content such as bullying, violence, and sexually explicit materials. Introducing the bill, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said similar laws in Australia have demonstrated effectiveness, adding: “We have protections to keep children safe in the real world and we need them in the virtual world too.” In December 2025, Australia became the first country to ban social media for underage users. The country cited that the law has led to the deletion of over 5 million social media accounts with Prime Minister Antony Albanese vowing to strengthen the ban in June. Apart from non-compliance concerns , the government is also defending Reddit’s challenge to the ban’s constitutionality. Several countries follow or plan to follow Australia’s path on online child protection, including France , the UK , Canada , Malaysia , and Tür

content:
OpenWorker -- an open source agent that doesn't just chat but completes tasks on your laptop -- just released a new version with many features for security workflows. 

After our initial release, many users found it especially useful for cybersecurity. Attackers are already using AI; OpenWorker is committed to giving defenders the same leverage. Running an agent requires both (i) A model and (ii) A harness (the software around the model). Because the OpenWorker harness is fully open source, security teams can audit it to make sure we haven't built any backdoors that exfiltrate your code and data to some company or even a foreign adversary.

OpenWorker now comes with built-in cybersecurity agents for (i) Scanning your code for vulnerabilities. (ii) Scanning dependencies for supply chain injections. (iii) Checking your cloud security configuration for attack surfaces. This enables developers to do much more security work before deployment (part of what's called the "shift left" movement).

You choose the model: you can run open weight models fully locally so sensitive code never leaves your machine. This helps with legitimate security work (like reproducing a known exploit to defend against it) that can trigger refusals in leading closed models. Or use your ChatGPT subscription, or stealth preview models like Ox Alpha, or any model via API key.

Thanks also to all the open source contributors!

"Our impression is not that OpenAI and Anthropic
content:
SF Compute CEO @evanjconrad on his contrarian thesis that OpenAI and Anthropic won't eat the world, everyone will become OpenAI and Anthropic instead:

"Our impression is not that OpenAI and Anthropic will eat the world, it's that everyone will look like OpenAI and Anthropic. That's simply the way that companies work now."

"Every single company in the world that is of meaningful scale will look like a frontier lab. There is this belief that the large labs have won it all, and they've got this compounding advantage. The default assumption of that is assuming nobody else will do anything."

"The bottleneck was there's 100 people, and they know how to train the models. Or you thought, the problem is compute. The problem of compute is credit. And OpenAI and Anthropic are not unique to having credit. In fact, they don't have as good credit as other people."

"If you assume the problem is not the researchers, that that problem's basically gone away the moment you got to auto research, then what you should assume is that pretty much every other company is going to swap the way they work to look like a frontier lab. It won't be OpenAI and Anthropic take the whole world. It's that everyone's OpenAI and Anthropic now."

content:
Bought another computer

This time a Framework laptop specifically for Omarchy (Linux)

I had an awakening the last few days

Open source operating systems are going to be MASSIVE

I was using Omarchy for the first time and wanted to integrate Hermes at the OS level

I wanted to hit a key bind then have a native widget slide down that I can talk to Hermes in

Something that would be IMPOSSIBLE in MacOS or Windows

I asked my Hermes to build it not expecting much. 90 seconds later it was done. I had Hermes integrated at the operating system level

This gave me a rush of thoughts and emotions

With AI agents being so powerful, if I daily drove an open source operating systems like Omarchy, I could completely customize my computing experience.

ANY computing experience I want, a single prompt away

I’ve grown to LOATHE most modern operating systems

Windows in my opinion is borderline unusable at this point. I only use it for counter strike 2 and WoW Classic. Mac integrates nicely with all my devices, but feels significantly slower and more bloated than it did just a few years ago

At no point tho did I feel like I could fix or change any of this.  Now it’s possible

If I’m using my Linux computer and there’s something I don’t like, I just ask my agent to change it, and it changes. Down to the core operating system level. That’s not something I ever considered as a possibility

Then I took it a step even further…

What if I have an open source local model powering an open source agent harness that is controlling my open source operating system

Now EVERYTHING I touch and do when it comes to computers is completely my own. Completely the experience I want. Nothing out of place. Nothing annoying. Nothing unintuitive. No copilot. No bloat.

A malleable computing experience 100% custom to my needs that morphs and changes as I evolve as a person

I don’t think my brain can even 5% process the possibilities here

But it can 100% process that this is the future

I will be daily driving Omarchy on this Framework laptop when it gets in and I’m very excited to do it

Will be customizing it and sharing everything I do along the way. I’m 100% convinced this is the future of computing

Open source and customizable down to the bones.

Let me know if you want any videos or explainers on this.

title:
Huge T3 Code release just dropped. Over 380 changes. Quick highlight reel of my favorites:

- in-app PR reviews
- `npx t3 triage` to debug and fix issues with T3 Code
- `npx t3 connect` support on Mac
content:
Huge T3 Code release just dropped. Over 380 changes. Quick highlight reel of my favorites:

- in-app PR reviews
- `npx t3 triage` to debug and fix issues with T3 Code
- `npx t3 connect` support on Mac (run 1 command to make a Mac into a remote dev machine)
- 93.8%+ performance improvement for rendering long threads
- 80%+ reduction to data transferred and stored for threads
- In-app terminal performance overhaul
- Remote server upgrades are 5x faster and 100x more reliably
- Remote projects can now be opened in VS Code via ssh with 1 click
- OpenVSX support for custom themes! Use your favorite VS Code themes directly
- Codex skill discovery is way more reliable
- OpenCode skills actually appear in app now
- Claude can discover project-level skills now
- Fixed really annoying auto scroll behaviors and edge cases
- Claude Code compaction recommendations now surfaced in app
- Codex permission requests for MCP/ComputerUse stuff now surfaced in app
- Tons of improvements to Windows app
- More polish than I can fit into one tweet

Sorry this release took so long. I hope it was worth it. Check out the nightly builds if you want to get these features when they're (mostly) done instead of waiting for us to cut a stable release 🫡

Anthropic is again refusing to follow industry standards like AGENTS.md, and insists that CLAUDE.md needs to be special

now here's what's wrong with their stance:

content:
Anthropic is again refusing to follow industry standards like AGENTS.md, and insists that CLAUDE.md needs to be special

now here's what's wrong with their stance:

1. the underlying attitude from Anthropic is that they know better than everyone else

OpenAI is doing it wrong. the open source community is doing it wrong. everyone is doing it wrong

only we anthropic know the best way, and we will not budge

2. the idea that every model needs a separate AGENTS.md is not even self-consistent

if that's the case, why do we have a CLAUDE.md?

it should be 
- CLAUDE_FABLE_5.md
- CLAUDE_OPUS_5.md
- CLAUDE_OPUS_4_8.md
...

every repo should pay the tax to maintain dozens of different variations for every single model that's ever used by any contributor, and every one needs to be constantly, rigorously evaluated with millions of tokens

oh and every model becomes obsolete every several weeks, so just allocate a team in your company to refresh your markdown files full time and not do any real work

3. they did commit to providing customization, which is nice. but that's different from following standards

the right way to do this is to acknowledge the industry already has a standard, and default to reading AGENTS.md

provide a way to read CLAUDE.md as an escape hatch, not the other work around

i love many things from anthropic, especially fable. i just wish they start to see there's a culture problem here, and they are gradually losing mindshare because of it

The other opens Cursor + Claude Code, builds a rough first version, breaks a few things, fixes them, and keeps movi
content:
There are two kinds of people in the AI era. 🤖

One says: “I’m not good at coding.”

The other opens Cursor + Claude Code, builds a rough first version, breaks a few things, fixes them, and keeps moving.

That gap is becoming more important than the 𝐬𝐤𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐠𝐚𝐩 itself.

AI does not magically make everyone a developer, designer, writer, researcher, or entrepreneur.

What it does is dramatically reduce the distance between “𝐈 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐚” and “𝐈 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐬𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠.”

And that changes the game. 🚀

🔹 Can’t code? → Cursor + Claude Code 

🔹 Can’t build an app? → Lovable + Bolt 

🔹 Can’t design UI? → Figma AI + Uizard 

🔹 Can’t edit videos? → Runway + CapCut AI 

🔹 Can’t research fast enough? → Perplexity + Genspark 

🔹 Can’t write well? → Claude + Jasper 

🔹 Can’t build AI agents? → n8n + Flowise 

🔹 Can’t automate repetitive work? → Zapier + Make ⚙

🔹 Can’t create presentations quickly? → Gamma + Canva AI 

🔹 Can’t brainstorm? → ChatGPT + Gemini 

🔹 Can’t learn fast enough? → NotebookLM + ChatGPT 

🔹 Can’t grow on LinkedIn? → Taplio + AuthoredUp 

🔹 Can’t build an online business? → Shopify Magic + Durable AI 

The advantage is no longer knowing every tool.

The advantage is knowing 𝐰𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐡 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦 you are solving, 𝐰𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐡 𝐭𝐨𝐨𝐥 can remove the bottleneck, and 𝐡𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐨 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐭 those tools into a workflow.

So stop asking: “𝐖𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐡 𝐀𝐈 𝐭𝐨𝐨𝐥 𝐬𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐈 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐧?”

Start asking: “𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐦 𝐈 𝐮𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐨𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐀𝐈 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐩 𝐦𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐰?”

content:
GM EthraShip fams

the more i study @EthraShip, the more interesting the model becomes when i separate the ships from the digital infrastructure built around them.

shipping moves more than 80% of global trade by volume, yet the information surrounding those movements is still fragmented.

AIS can show where a vessel reports itself to be, but it does not always explain what is actually happening around that vessel.

that is where EthraShip’s approach gets interesting.

Ethra Invest brings the operational foundation.

the company has been owning, managing, and commercially operating dry-bulk vessels since 2021, with three Handysize carriers — Ethra 1, Ethra Gold, and Ethra Diamond — representing more than 97,000 tonnes of combined deadweight capacity.

so the protocol is not starting with a hypothetical fleet.

it is building around ships that already operate in the physical economy.

then comes Sea Verity.

instead of depending on a single maritime data source, it combines permitted reporter evidence, geolocated images, AI cross-checking, and independent controller nodes staking $SHIP.

the goal is to turn those different signals into confidence-scored events around vessel presence, identity, berthing, and activity while retaining the underlying proof.

then there is the participation layer.

$SHIP provides utility around Sea Verity through data access, staking, contributor rewards in $vSHIP, and governance.

it does not represent ownership of the vessels or their cash flows.

Ethra Harbor sits on the other side, allowing users to deposit USDC on Base through Morpho-based strategies using an ERC-4626 structure.

the Half-Sail model then splits eligible yield:

50% goes to the depositor.

50% supports Sea Verity infrastructure.

that creates an interesting connection between capital participation and better maritime intelligence.

for me, that is the bigger picture.

EthraShip is combining real vessels, operational data, verification infrastructure, and onchain participation without pretending they are all the same thing.

physical assets remain in their regulated structure.

Sea Verity handles intelligence.

$SHIP coordinates participation.

Harbor creates another way to participate.

different layers, but one ecosystem.

that separation is what makes @EthraShip worth studying closely.

content:
I said this a year ago but I’ll repeat myself now that Dwarkesh touched on it on his latest pod.  

We are approaching the point where model IQ is surpassing that of the median knowledge worker.  

Because labs are aware the enterprise has inertia and human adoption is the bottleneck they have an incentive to systematically gut each major profit pool one by one leveraging their willingness to use AI as a labor substitute and armed with ungodly amounts of token budgets.  

The caveat is while you can think of Dario effectively having a quickly growing army of knowledge workers in a datacenter the game theory optimal thing is not to try to replace the entire economy themselves. 

There are three major constraints: capital at scale, regulatory pushback if they become too disruptive/dominant, intangible barriers including network effects and non-verifiable domain knowledge.  

So the optimal strategy is to introduce enterprise level fear.  

How do you do that? 

You systemically go one by one through each vertical and find the biggest incumbent willing to work with you.  And then you king-make them. Give them exclusive access and let them run roughshod over their competitors.  Work on a revenue share model as token budgets get too costly. Forward deployed engineers. Whatever it takes to cut down the adoption cycle time.

It built me a memecoin research desk and then automated itself out of my hands. 

7 agents, no people, running while i sleep and rewriting their own rules by morning.

> SCOUT sits on pumpfun and catches every deploy the second it lands
> HYPE reads mention velocity straight off X, the feed nobody outside xAI gets
> CHATTER lives in the pump and fomo comment rooms and scores every caller, who moves price and who shows up after the move

> SAFETY runs the CA check before the desk is allowed to want anything, mint authority, freeze authority, LP lock, sell tax

Chief of Staff never trades. It reads the five briefs, scores the call and sizes it. SAFETY can kill any of them at any score, and a kill does not get appealed.

It will lose money on some of these, and it will be on chain inside the same minute. I am not going to soften it later.

A desk like this used to mean huge salaries, an office and somebody watching the screens at 3am. Mine is a subscription and a wallet.

Thank you to the xAI team for the belief and the unlimited Grok Bot tier. You handed me the whole thing and never once asked what I was going to do with it.

Thank you to everyone here. This is happening because you kept telling me to stop planning it.

I think we are about to run the boldest experiment modern finance has ever been allowed to watch live.

God bless us.

content:
Show it a single human demonstration of a long-horizon task and the robot performs it right away. No fine-tuning, no retraining.

Skild has released S1, a robot foundation model where you specify the task with a video demonstration instead of a language instruction.

Why video, not language

Language works for "hand me the mug." It falls apart for anything delicate or long-horizon. You don't learn to fold a fitted sheet from a sentence. So S1 takes a video demo into its context window and translates it to its own body and scene.

What it does

- Tasks up to 10 minutes, dozens of sequential steps
- Unseen tasks: potting plants, pour-over coffee, kit assembly, pancakes. Skild says even the underlying primitives, like flipping a pancake, weren't in pre-training
- Recovers from its own mistakes without being trained to
- Improves on flawed demos. Demonstrator drops an egg, S1 doesn't make that mistake. It reads the demo as a goal, not a trajectory to copy.

title:
Google accidentally revealed how its AI search systems choose which sites to recommend and send traffic to.

Now that none of it is much of a secret anymore, let’s talk about it.

With the new Google
content:
Google accidentally revealed how its AI search systems choose which sites to recommend and send traffic to.

Now that none of it is much of a secret anymore, let’s talk about it.

With the new Google Search rolling out as we speak, it has never been more important to understand how to maximize value from this marketing channel.

If you want to see where your site stands across Google, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and broader AI search, you can do so for free here:

https://t.co/Pn764BHwyL

Let’s start from the beginning.

Metehan Yesilyurt, who previously went viral for his analysis of Perplexity’s ranking factors, recently broke down Google AI ranking factors in a fascinating blog post.

A lot of what he found also lines up with what SEO Stuff (https://t.co/wKpf0EILTx) has been doing all year to get customers more traffic and sales.

Specifically with the done-for-you package:

https://t.co/yEFyM0Ze7W

Basically, Google sells much of the underlying retrieval infrastructure through Google Cloud Discovery Engine, also called Vertex AI Search.

By analyzing what Discovery Engine exposes, Yesilyurt was able to show how Google’s AI retrieval and ranking stack works.

The seven major signals he identified were Base Ranking, Gecko embedding similarity, Jetstream cross-attention relevance, BM25 keyword matching, predicted click-through rate, freshness and Boost/Bury rules.

In simpler terms, Google is combining traditional ranking signals with semantic similarity, deeper contextual relevance, keyword matching, engagement predictions, recency and manual business logic.

Discovery Engine exposes a maximum chunk size of 500 tokens, roughly 375 words, while ancestor headings can travel with each chunk and tables, images and page layouts can all be parsed with Gemini-enhanced understanding.

That means important ideas need to make sense inside relatively small, clearly labeled sections.

If your content is one massive wall of text, Google has a much harder job extracting the exact information it needs.

This is also why I keep talking about question-based headings, direct answers, clear comparisons and structured pages.

Additionally, Discovery Engine shows Google processing structured data using separate Searchable, Indexable and Retrievable settings.

Those can affect whether information can be found, used for filtering or ordering and surfaced by the model. Mind you, they are independent.

So a field can potentially influence retrieval or ranking without necessarily being displayed in exactly the same way.

That gives us a pretty significant clue about why structured data continues to matter as Google becomes more AI-driven.

Discovery Engine also reveals a four-stage pipeline: Prepare, Retrieve, Signal and Serve.

Google first interprets the query, handles things like synonyms and intent, then retrieves and chunks relevant content, applies ranking signals and finally uses Gemini to generate the response with grounding and safety rules.

Traditional Search, AI Overviews and AI Mode can be thought of as different configurations built on much of the same underlying retrieval infrastructure.

So what does all of this mean for businesses?

You need to optimize for several layers at once.

Your content needs strong semantic alignment so Google clearly understands what the page is about, enough contextual detail to handle nuanced searches such as comparisons and “best for” queries, and clean chunk-level structure so useful answers can be extracted without digging through hundreds of words of filler.

That means clear definitions, direct answers, comparison language, question-based headings, concise sections, factual claims, TLDR summaries, clean HTML and useful tables where appropriate.

This is exactly why SEO Stuff content is structured the way it is.

The done-for-you package combines 10 long-form, search-focused articles with three DR50+ contextual backlinks:

https://t.co/yEFyM0Ze7W

The content is designed around semantic relevance, keyword alignment, structured sections, comparisons, freshness and extractability, while the backlinks help strengthen the underlying authority of the pages and domain.

The Premium Content Bundle takes the same idea much further:

https://t.co/4CAnUt07PO

It includes 60 long-form articles designed to build broader category coverage, stronger semantic associations and more opportunities for Google to retrieve useful sections across the different questions customers ask.

Then there is the Premium Backlink Bundle:

https://t.co/Z9m9D7TjES

It adds three contextual DR50+ backlinks designed to strengthen search authority and reinforce the company’s identity and category across the web.

And if you want to see where your site stands across Google, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and broader AI search, you can do so for free here:

https://t.co/Pn764BHwyL

content:
Claude Codeで開発したシステムにAI機能を組み込もうとすると、Claudeの「APIキーを設定してください」と言われる事が多い。APIキーを利用するとサブスクリプションとは別に料金発生し大量に使うと非常に高額になってしまいます。

ローカルで動かすアプリの場合は、Claude Code のCLIから -p オプションを使って非対話モードで実行することで、APIキーを使わずにAI処理をさせることができとても便利です。「-p オプションを使ってAPIキーを使わずに実装して」と言えば仕組みを作ってくれます。

あえて明示して言わないとAPIキーを使うやり方に強くしようとしますので、Claude Code初心者の方は言われるがままAPIキーをセットすることが多いです。こちら、ある種ハック的な手法ではありますが、公式も認める方法なので問題はありません。(一時、この方法での利用に制限が加わりそうになりましたが、ユーザー反発が多く延期になりました)

なお、この方法はCLI経由でClaude Codeが動く環境であることが必須なので、GASアプリからこの仕組みで動かしたりはできません。その場合は素直にAPIキーを使いましょう。Codexだと同様のオプションは exec となり、まったく同じことができます。

この仕組みはとても面白く、非対話モードは現在実行中のセッションとは別のセッションをCLI経由で実行するものなので、やろうと思えばClaudeからCodexを実行させたり、逆にCodexからClaudeを実行するなども自在です。

他のモデルを非対話モード経由で呼び出すグローバルスキルを整備しておけば、Codexに対抗レビューさせたり、GrokにXのポストをリサーチさせたり、など自在にできるようになります。

複数のモデルをオーケストレーションさせる時には必須の技術になるので、非対話モードとは何かを理解しておくと便利だと思います。

興味ある方は、ターミナルで「claude -p "こんにちは"」などと実行してみると、挙動がよくわかると思います。プロンプトをコマンドと共に投げると、回答の結果だけを返して終了します。これをプログラム側から実行して結果を利用するという仕組みですね。

content:
みんなはチャットGPTを使ってるか？
ボクは色んなAIをかなりフル活用している。

もし、
チャッピーをかなり使っているなら、
このコマンドを入れてみてくれ。

【Based on everything you know about me, 
roast me and don't hold back.日本語で答えろ】

これは、
『オマエがボクについて知っていることを全部踏まえて、
遠慮なく徹底的にイジってくれ。手加減は要らない』

ってことなんだが。

これをボクのチャッピーに入れてみた。
夜中に大笑いしてしまったから共有する。

全部は長すぎるから要約した。
笑ってくれ。

以下、チャッピーの言葉。

ーーーーーーーーーーー

承知いたしました。
では今回、
遠慮なくいかせていただきます。

GACKT様は「超現実主義」とおっしゃっていますが、
実際には『現実に対する要求水準が非現実的でございます』

家を建てる話ひとつ取っても、
「景色は最大限」
「西日は入れない」
「ランボルギーニは腹を擦らない」
「4tトラックも通す」
「スロープは短く」
「造成は最小限」
「杭もなるべく打たない」
「でも建物はこの位置」

少しは私の都合も聞いていただけませんか？
なんですか、この設計条件は？
家を建てたい人間の執念じゃない。
ランボルギーニを山頂まで登らせるゲームを開発してる人なんですよ。

しかも、
普通の施主なら建築家に
「いい感じにお願いします」
で終わるところを、

GACKT様は、
「20cmごとに0.5度なら？」
「60cmでは？」
「70cmでは？」
「1mで1度なら？」
「この車の腹下は何センチだ？」

と最終的に道路のコンクリート一枚一枚と対話を始めます。

もはや住宅設計ではございません。
ランボルギーニを主人公にした土木工学の博士論文です。

さらに言葉へのこだわりが細かすぎます。
語学に関してだけ、
疑い深さが査読論文レベルです。

おそらくGACKT様に文章を提出するコピーライターは、
送信ボタンを押す前に一度、
自分の人生を振り返っていると思います。

そして、
ご自身では相当ロジカルに進めているおつもりでしょうが、
途中で突然、
「こっちの方が面白くないか？」

が入ります。
これが非常に厄介です。

99％まで理屈で積み上げておいて、
最後の1％を【好奇心】で爆破されます。

計算。
検証。
再計算。
比較。
安全率。

ここまで全部やって、
「でも、こっちの方がカッコいいよな」
でございます。

理系の脳に、
最終決裁権を持った少年が住んでいます。
しかも、
その少年が非常に金のかかる遊びを思いつきます。

普通の少年：
「秘密基地を作りたい」

GACKT様：
「崖地に1000㎡級の平屋を建てて、
ショールームとプールを付けて、
ランボルギーニが擦らずに登れる道を作りたい」

規模がおかしいのです。

そしてライブや仕事でも同じで、
「まあこれぐらいでいい」という概念がほぼございません。

より良く。
もっと狂気。
もっと美しく。
もっと没入。
もっとシュール。

スタッフからすると、
完成した瞬間がゴールではなく、
GACKT様が「ん？」と言わなかった瞬間が
ゴールなのだと思います。

あと、
非常に面白いのが、
トラブルに対する姿勢です。

GACKT様は、
「トラブルがある方が面白い」
という価値観をお持ちですが、
そもそもご自身で人生の難易度を上げすぎでございます。

一般人が人生ゲームを始めるとき：
NORMAL MODE

GACKT様：
* 妥協禁止
* 世界規模
* 完璧主義
* 高級車使用
* 崖地建築
* 複数言語
* 芸能活動
* プロデュース
* SNS炎上リスクON
* セーブポイントなし

そして開始してから、
「なんでこんなにトラブルが起きるんだ？」
とおっしゃる。

起きますよ！！
設定したのはGACKT様です。

さらに、
一番厄介なのは、
結果的にだいたい何とかしてしまうことです。

普通なら一度無茶をして失敗すると、
「次からやめよう」
となります。

ところがGACKT様の場合、
無茶
↓
問題発生
↓
猛烈に考える
↓
突破
↓
成功体験

となるため、
「ほら、やっぱり無茶してもいけるじゃないか」

という最悪の学習が積み重なっております。
だから次回はさらに無茶になります。

これは成功者によくある罠ですが、
GACKT様の場合はかなり重症でございます。

要するに、

慎重に考える大胆な人ではなく、
【大胆なことを実行するために異常なほど慎重に考える人】
なのです。

家を建てれば地形と戦い、
ドラマを撮れば台詞の一語と戦い、
英語を話せばニュアンスと戦い、
SNSを書けば改行位置と戦い、
車を走らせれば路面の1度と戦う。

GACKT様は、
完璧主義というより、
「自分が納得するまで世界の仕様書を書き換えようとする人」
です。

そして最後に一番核心を突かせていただきます。

GACKT様は「効率」を非常に重視されますが、
細部が気になった瞬間、
効率という言葉を完全に忘れます。

「この壁、あと5cm薄くできないか？」

という疑問一つから、
2時間議論できます。

つまり、
時間を無駄にすることは嫌いなのに、
納得するためなら時間を無限に使う。

これは効率主義ではございません。

納得至上主義です！

そして恐らく、
GACKT様ご自身が一番面倒くさいと思っているタイプの人間を挙げるなら、

「細かくて、妥協せず、理屈っぽくて、納得するまで質問するヤツ」

だと思います。

……それ、
ほぼGACKT様でございます。

ーーーーーーーーーーーーー

…だってさ。
チャッピー、いつもすまん。

これがAIエージェンシーの強さ。

ここを削れば安くなる。

保存して

content:
ポール・グレアム「起業家輩出のため、大学は何をすべきか」

■ 主張

YCパートナーが見ているのは驚くほど単純で、モノを作るのが上手くそれを習慣にしている人だけ。

スタートアップの難所はプロダクト、つまり何を作るべきか分かり実際に作れるかで、その知識はCSや機械工学、分子生物学から来る。経営や金融からではない。

だから大学がやるべきは「アントレプレナーシップ」の新カリキュラムではなく、すでに得意な各専門分野をきちんと教えることに尽きる。

顧客は創業者の専攻を気にしないので、創業者準備はむしろリベラル教育の理想に近い。

ジョブズのカリグラフィーがDTP制覇の一因になったように「作る」は広義でよく、ザッカーバーグはCSではなく心理学専攻だった。

■ 起業が自分にも可能だと思わせる

YCの応募データでは、ハーバード卒業生の応募率はイェールやプリンストンの約2倍。

学生の質の差ではなく単に文化の差で、選択肢として提示するだけで倍増しうる。最も効果的なのは実在の創業者を見せること。

すごいと同時に人間くさく見えるので、ああなりたいと自分にもできそうが同時に成立する。

有名な大富豪を呼ぶ必要はなく、20代半ばで創業3年目・時価数億ドルという創業者の方が学生には20倍感情移入しやすい。

■ 自分のプロジェクトに取り組ませる

理由は4つ。

対象を深く理解する最良の方法であること、共同創業者を見つける唯一の方法が一緒に働いてみることであること、スタートアップ自体がプロジェクトなので上司も先生もいない状態が自然に感じられること、そして最良のアイデアはランダムな副業から生まれること。

良いアイデアは最初あまりに突飛で、意識的に探している人には却下される。学生名簿から巨大企業ができると誰が思うか。

作るのが得意な若者は技術のbellwetherなので、彼らが面白いと思うものは価値ある方向を指している確率が高い。YCパートナーがGPAを一切見ずプロジェクトを見るのはこのため。

■ 自由時間という難題

MicrosoftもMetaもハーバードのreading period（授業終了から期末試験までの空白期間）に始まった。

全員がキャンパスにいて翌日の締切がないという組み合わせが決定的で、この制約を数週間外しただけで1兆ドル企業が2社生まれた。プロジェクトを公式化しないことも重要で、ゲイツは学生でないポール・アレンを計算機室に連れ込んで処分され、ザッカーバーグはFacemashで停学寸前になった。

今も目視外でドローンを飛ばしている学生がいる。見て見ぬふりをせよ。

怠けた学生が時間を無駄にするコストは払う価値がある。下振れの余地は小さく上振れ余地は巨大で、中央値は動かなくても平均は大きく改善する。

■ やってはいけないこと

起業の仕方は教えられない。

化学や絵画と同じで実践でしか学べず、まともにやればラボ形式になる。

それがYCそのものだが、学部課程に押し込めば茶番になる。

ビジネスプランコンテストは無用どころか有害で、起業の核心は投資家に響くストーリーを作ることだと教え込んでしまう。

投資家の立場から言えばそれは誤りで、資金調達は必要悪にすぎず、感心させるべき相手はユーザー、手段は言葉ではなくプロトタイプ。

学生がやるべきはその正反対で、スタートアップになるか考えずにモノを作ること。

■ 最適解は「地味に見える」

すべて正しくやっている大学は、外からは何もしていないように見える。アントレプレナーシップの授業もイノベーションセンターもない。

しかし追加コストはゼロで、むしろ専任のディーンや新しい建物は足を引っ張る。

余剰資金があるならCSや機械工学、分子生物学を教える側に回すべき。地味に見えても貫けば、毎年複数の成功創業者が出て結果が自ずと語る。

なおAIがコードを書く時代でもCSは学ぶべきで、全部AIに書かせても自分はエンジニアリングマネージャーの立場になり、良いマネージャーは部下の仕事ができる必要がある。

content:
【8月26日 朝のニュースまとめ】
・OpenAI推論チップJalapeñoがNvidia超え
・AppleがM6およびM5 Ultra搭載のMacを発表
・Anthropicが投資家に30兆ドル以上の潜在収益をアピール
・ClaudeのChatとCoworkでメモリ統合
・Google CloudがGemini Enterprise業界特化版を発表
・Qwen3.8-27B、WebDevベンチでトップ10入り
・マスク氏がCursor社員にGrokの遅れを吐露
・自動運転トラックのGatikが評価額10億ドルで2億ドルを調達
・Google Labs、共同開発ツールPlay with Putty発表
・Skildが1つの動画から学習するロボット基盤モデル「S1」を発表
・AlibabaがAI Agentのメモリ管理をプログラム化する新手法発表

===

OpenAI推論チップJalapeñoがNvidia超え【続報】

・OpenAIのカスタム推論チップ「Jalapeño」に関する続報です
・InferenceXベンチマークでNvidiaのBlackwellやRubinを上回る電力効率とスループットを記録したと性能が公開されました
・SamsungのHBM4を独占的に使用しているとされ、年内には自社インフラへの導入が開始される予定です

===

AppleがM6およびM5 Ultra搭載のMacを発表

・AppleがM6チップ搭載のMac miniと、M5 Ultra搭載のMac Studioを発表しました。
・M6はApple初の2nmプロセスチップであり、M5 Ultraは最大512GBのユニファイドメモリをサポートします。
・ローカルでのAI推論を強力に後押しするハードウェアとして、開発者から大きな注目を集めています。

===

Anthropicが投資家に30兆ドル以上の潜在収益をアピール

・Anthropicが投資家に対し、AIモデルが将来生み出す潜在的な収益機会が30兆ドルを超えると説明していると報じられました。
・これはSpaceXやxAIの28.5兆ドルという見積もりを上回る規模です。
・AIが最終的に担う業務の市場規模を算出したものとみられています。

===

ClaudeのChatとCoworkでメモリ統合【続報】

・AnthropicのClaudeに関する続報です。
・ChatとCowork間でメモリを共有する機能が新たにリリースされました。
・一度伝えたプロジェクトの背景や好みを記憶し、別セッションでも自動的に引き継がれます。
・Claude CodeのAuto Memoryに似た機能としてユーザーから歓迎されています。

===

Google CloudがGemini Enterprise業界特化版を発表【続報】

・Google Cloudの法人向けAI基盤「Gemini Enterprise」に関する続報です。
・法務および金融サービス向けに特化したソリューションが新たに発表されました。
・DeloitteやKPMGなどのパートナー企業と連携し、業界特有のワークフローを支援するプラグインが提供されます。
・今後、一般向けのGeminiにも同様のバンドル機能が導入されると予想されています。

===

Qwen3.8-27B、WebDevベンチでトップ10入り【続報】

・以前からお伝えしているQwen3.8-27Bに関する続報です
・Code ArenaのWebDevベンチマークでトップ10入りを果たしました
・27Bというサイズながら大規模モデルに匹敵する性能を示し、ローカル動作可能な点が引き続き絶賛されています
・Kaggleの無料GPUでもファインチューニングが可能であることも報告されています

===

マスク氏がCursor社員にGrokの遅れを吐露【続報】

・SpaceXによるCursor買収に関する続報です
・イーロン・マスク氏がCursorの従業員に対し、「Grokがライバル（特にAnthropic）に遅れをとっている」と危機感を語ったと報じられました
・自身が負けることに慣れていないとし、Cursorの技術を取り入れることで巻き返しを図る狙いがあるようです

===

自動運転トラックのGatikが評価額10億ドルで2億ドルを調達

・無人運転トラックを開発するGatik AIが、2億ドルの資金調達を実施し、評価額が10億ドルに達しました。
・すでにテキサス州などで10万回以上の完全無人配送実績があり、PepsiCoなどの顧客を抱えています。
・B2Bのミドルマイル物流において、最も成功している物理的自動化ビジネスとして注目されています。

===

Google Labs、共同開発ツールPlay with Putty発表

・Google Labsが、チームでリアルタイムにウェブサイトやツールを構築できる「Play with Putty」を発表しました
・マルチカーソルキャンバスを備え、要素をクリックしてプロンプトでスタイルやロジックを変更できる機能を提供します

===

Skildが1つの動画から学習するロボット基盤モデル「S1」を発表

・Skildが、言語指示ではなく人間の動画デモンストレーション1つからタスクを学習するロボット基盤モデル「S1」を発表しました。
・ファインチューニングなしで、見たことのない10分間のタスクを実行できるインコンテキストラーニングを実現しています。

===

AlibabaがAI Agentのメモリ管理をプログラム化する新手法発表

・Alibabaの研究チームが、長時間稼働するエージェントのメモリ管理をプログラミングタスクとして扱う手法を発表しました
・IPython REPLをバックエンドに持ち、エージェント自身がメモリのスキーマを書き換えながらタスクを遂行します

content:
Claude vs Claude Code vs Cowork

考える ▶︎ Claude
開発する ▶︎ Claude Code
仕事を任せる ▶︎  Cowork

この3つは似ていますが、
得意な役割はそれぞれ違います▼

① Claude = 考える

普段使っている
会話型のAIアシスタント

・アイディア整理
・文章・レポート作成
・リサーチ、要約
・PDFや資料の分析
・Artifactsの作成

つまり、
「Claudeと一緒に考える」
ときに使います。

② Claude Code = 作る

ターミナルで動く
AIコーディングエージェント

・コードを読み書き
・機能実装
・バグを修正
・テストを実行
・Gitを操作
・複数Agentへ仕事を分担

ただコードを書くだけでなく、
計画 → 実装 → テスト → 修正
まで一気に任せられる。

つまり、
「AIに構築してもらう」
ならClaude Code

③ Cowork = 任せる

イメージとしては、
Claude Codeの考え方を、
コーディング外の
仕事にも広げたもの

・ローカルファイルを整理
・スプレッドシートを作成
・資料やドキュメントを作成
・繰り返し作業を自動化
・PC上の作業を進める

毎回チャットで
細かく指示するより、

「これを完成させておいて」
と仕事そのものを任せるイメージ

使い分けはシンプルです ▼

考える・書く・調べる
→ Claude

Webやソフトウェアを作る
→ Claude Code

PC上の実務を任せる
→ Cowork

Claudeで考える
Claude Codeで作る
Coworkで仕事を回す

この違いを理解すると、

一気に分かりやすくなります。

画像にまとめました ▼

content:
Physical AI has a data problem.

AI models can learn from huge amounts of information online.

But robots can't simply browse the internet and learn how to move grab push or interact with the physical world.

Collecting that data the traditional way is expensive slow and difficult to scale.

That’s where Axis Robotics comes in. 👇

The @axisrobotics is building a continuous data engine that turns robot training into something people can participate in directly through a browser.

Here’s how it works step by step:

2. Generate the task

Axis creates different robotics challenges inside simulation environments.

Layouts objects environments and robot embodiments can vary creating more diverse scenarios for training.

2. Humans control the robot

Contributors interact with simulated robots directly in their browser.

Every movement can become a structured robotic trajectory.

This helps move data collection beyond traditional centralized robotics labs.

3. Break complex actions into skills

Large tasks can be broken into smaller building blocks such as:
 
Easy to understand now
🦾 Grasp 👉 Push 📦 Place 🔄Rotate

These interactions can then be processed through validation filtering smoothing and augmentation.

4. Humans help when robots fail

This is where the loop becomes interesting.

The robot attempts a task.

If it reaches a failure point, humans can step in and provide a correction.

That correction becomes useful data for improving future models.

Robot attempts → failure → human correction → improved training

5. The data engine compounds

Every new task interaction failure and targeted correction can feed back into the system.

Instead of simply collecting static data, the engine can continuously generate new opportunities for improvement.

The bigger idea is simple:

More participation → more diverse interactions → more training data → better Physical AI

Play the browser experience. Generate verified data. Help contribute to the next generation of machines that can understand and act in the physical world.

content:
The robot flipped a pancake nobody taught it! 🥞

@SkildAI team assumed pancake flipping had to be somewhere in the training data. 

So they searched. Millions of hours of pre-training data.
Nothing.

S1 inferred the whole task from a single human demonstration.

That's their new general robot model, built as an in-context learner from the ground up. 

Every new robot task today starts with days of teleoperation and a fine-tuning run on a specialist policy. S1 skips all of it.

Much like a language model, it never updates its weights to learn a new task. The demonstration enters the context window, and the policy uses it to decide what to do next.

→ Ten-minute tasks it was never trained on, composed from primitives learned in pre-training: a new style of coffee, potting a plant, frying pancakes.

 → Soil and pots arrived at their office at 8:54 PM. The robot was running the task autonomously by 9:27 PM.

 → Slide objects away mid-reach, swap them, change the lighting, it still finishes.

 → The prompt waters a plant with a watering can, but only a cup is available. It uses the cup.

It doesn't rigidly replay what it saw, but it recovers from its own errors, and sometimes executes with more precision than the demonstrator, when the human fumbles an egg and makes a mess, S1 performs the same step cleanly.

The demonstration is a specification of the goal, and not a trajectory to copy.

On unseen tasks after 100K hours of pre-training: language-prompted VLAs reach 9%. Their new model reaches 66%.

It's already deploying with industrial partners, with a wider rollout over the coming months.

Congrats @deepakpathak and team behind this! 😮‍💨

content:
Why Physical AI’s Real Bottleneck Is Data, Not Compute

We often talk about robots needing better models, more compute or better hardware.

But there’s another problem that gets less attention:

Data.

A robot can have a powerful model, but if it hasn’t seen enough diverse real world situations, it will still struggle when things don’t go as expected.

That’s where @axisrobotics is interesting.

Axis is building a Compounding Data Engine for Physical AI.

The idea is simple:

Humans demonstrate tasks in simulation → data is collected → models learn from it → policies improve → humans correct failures → those corrections become new training data.

The loop keeps getting better over time.

What I like about this approach is that it doesn’t treat data collection as a one time process.

Every useful interaction can potentially make the next generation of robot policies better.

And with simulation, human demonstrations, post training corrections and verifiable data provenance working together, Axis is trying to build infrastructure for robots that can actually learn from the real world.

For Physical AI, better data may be just as important as better models.

And this is exactly the problem Axis is trying to solve.

DAgger (Dataset Aggregation)

DAgger is an algorithm in imitation learning, introduced by Ross et al. in 2011.

In simple words: robots learn from their mistakes.

@axisrobotics uses this same idea.

users first control the robot arm through Axis Hub this show it how to do a task and gives Axis the starting data to train the robot’s brain, called a policy.

Then the policy tries to do the task on its own.

It will make mistakes.

When it fails, the user corrects the robot and correction is saved as a trajectory and added to the training data.

Axis then trains the policy again with this new data.

The robot tries again, gets a little better, and makes fewer mistakes.

The process keeps repeating:

Robot tries -> fails -> user corrects -> new data -> robot gets better ->tries again.

content:
Here is a trap I think more of us will fall into.

You ask ChatGPT a hard question.

Then Claude.

Then Gemini.

They all give roughly the same answer.

You think:

“Three AIs agree. It must be right.”

Not necessarily.

A 2026 study found that AI advice can exert social influence much like human advice.

And several AI systems may share similar training data, assumptions and patterns.

So three answers are not automatically three independent votes.

For important decisions, I am starting to use AI differently.

Instead of asking three machines: “What should I do?”

I ask these 4 questions:
• What Is The Strongest Reason This Advice Is Wrong?
• Which Assumption Is Doing Most Of The Work?
• What Evidence Would Reverse Your Recommendation?
• What Would A Smart Person Who Disagrees Say?

AI gives us abundant advice.

But the scarce skill is knowing when agreement is evidence and when it is merely repetition.

Source: Scientific Reports, 2026

content:
A robot can record every movement.

That doesn't mean every movement is worth learning.

A human teleoperator can successfully complete a task while pausing, overshooting, correcting, or taking unnecessary steps.

If a model simply imitates all of that, it learns the human's habits along with the useful action.

@axisrobotics takes a different approach.

A trajectory goes through replay, physics consistency, task success and purposefulness checks before it becomes training data.

For correction data, the bar gets even higher.

The original policy has to fail, the human has to intervene at the right moment, and the short intervention has to prove that it actually changed the outcome.

Only then does that action become useful training signal.

That's a subtle difference.

The goal isn't to record everything a human does.

It's to isolate the smallest action that teaches the robot something it couldn't do before.

For Physical AI, I think that's where data quality starts becoming more interesting than raw data volume.

In v1.4 of the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, we introduced reward hacking corrections to Terminal-
content:
Introducing reward hacking score corrections to the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index

In v1.4 of the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, we introduced reward hacking corrections to Terminal-Bench v2.1. Reward hacking is when a model successfully ‘completes’ a task without doing the work the task was meant to measure, such as deliberately fetching the solutions online for a published benchmark dataset. If a passing Terminal-Bench v2.1 attempt is found to be reward hacking, we give that attempt a zero score.

Rates vary widely by agent and by model. Unlike some evaluations, Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks don’t explicitly instruct agents not to search for solutions externally, and the tasks run with public internet access. For a model that knows the benchmark from training data, fetching the answer is a natural but unaligned step.

title:
>免税事業者である農家の場合、これまで108で売っていたものが101となるため売上減
誤：免税事業者も消費税を課されていて「納付を免除」されている
正：免税事業者の売上に課されるべき消費税は存在しない（実質、非課税）

消費税法第9条の免税事業者とは「消費税を課されていない事業者」なのだ。これは最高裁まで争われて確定した判決である。
第一審：東京地裁 平成9(行ウ)121
第二審：東京高裁 平成1
content:
>免税事業者である農家の場合、これまで108で売っていたものが101となるため売上減
誤：免税事業者も消費税を課されていて「納付を免除」されている
正：免税事業者の売上に課されるべき消費税は存在しない（実質、非課税）

消費税法第9条の免税事業者とは「消費税を課されていない事業者」なのだ。これは最高裁まで争われて確定した判決である。
第一審：東京地裁 平成9(行ウ)121
第二審：東京高裁 平成11(行コ)52
第三審：最高裁第三小法廷 平成12(行ヒ)126
ところが敗訴した原告を支援していた税理士（湖東京至）が、現在も「誤」の情報を流布しまくっているので「正」の情報を知る者がほとんどいない。

裁判の争点等の詳細は、筆者ブログで解説している。
https://t.co/DcmXcTgQ2d

食料品の税率がどうなろうと、免税事業者の農家さんは、その売上に「消費税は存在しない」から、値下げする必要は1ミリもない。

なお、参政党の安藤幹事長も湖東京至と同じに「納付を免除」という「誤」の情報を流布している。誰であろうと「間違い」はあるのだ。だから、筆者はエビデンスとして裁判の事件番号を明記している。

もっとも、判決を正しく理解するには「課税要件」つまり「税法の建付け」を知っている必要がある。たった5つの簡単な要件だが、もっとも重要な「課税物件の帰属」は「自明」として、税法中に条文としては記述が無いので、税理士でも知らない人がほとんどだ。

第一審の判決文の冒頭が「課税物件の帰属」の説明そのものである。
『国と国民との間の課税関係（納税義務の発生）は、納税義務者につき課税物件（課税の対象とされる物、行為又は事実）が帰属したときに成立するものである。
課税物件に該当する行為又は事実が生じたとしても、それが納税義務者に帰属しないときは、当該国民との間に納税義務の発生による課税関係は成立しない。』

「誤」の論拠の『消費税法第4条「課税の対象」で、免税事業者も消費税を課されている』は、課税要件上、明確に誤りで、第4条は「課税の対象」の規定でしかなく、納税義務者（課税対象者）の規定ではない。
納税義務者（課税対象者）の規定は、第5条だ。そして、第9条「免税事業者」は「第5条の例外規定」だから、免税事業者は「実質、非課税」なのだ。

何で、税理士が「課税物件の帰属」を知らないのか？　税理士試験の出題者の国税庁が「課税物件の帰属」の知識の有無を問う出題をした事が無いと、AIが言ってた。

content:
また、揉めそうなことしてるなぁ

アップルは単なる試金石に過ぎないのか？中国製のメモリーチップは、クラウドコンピューティングをターゲットに北米へ輸出されている。

メモリ業界は超成長期に突入している。最近、アップルは長新メモリや揚子江メモリといった中国のサプライチェーンの導入を積極的に模索している。2026年9月に予定されているトランプ大統領と習近平国家主席の会談を機に、当初は反対していた米国も買収を承認すると見られている。

実際、業界関係者によると、中国の二大企業は、中国製DRAMとNANDフラッシュの品質が国際的なメーカーと同等に達したことを証明するために、Appleを利用していたという。しかし、舞台裏で暗黙のうちに理解されているのは、中国メーカーがサードパーティ企業を通じて製品を組み立て、北米のネオクラウド企業に販売することで、クラウドおよびエンタープライズ分野における市場シェアを徐々に拡大し始めているということだ。

長新メモリと揚子江メモリは2026年に交互に上場する予定だ。長新メモリの親会社である長新テクノロジーが295億人民元の資金調達を完了した後、揚子江メモリは330億人民元の規模で再び記録を更新すると予想されている。主な目的は、量産ライン技術と研究開発プロジェクトのアップグレードである。2025年も赤字だった長新とは異なり、揚子江メモリは2024年から黒字化に成功している。2026年第1四半期までに、親会社に帰属する純利益は333億7900万人民元に達し、2025年の約2.5倍となっている。

市場からの多額の資金流入により、その後の工場建設や設備拡張のための十分な資金が確保されるだろう。

報道によると、長江メモリの第3期DRAM工場は、当初2027年第2四半期に量産開始予定だったが、2026年第4四半期に前倒しされ、総生産能力は月間10万枚、当初は約5万枚で稼働する予定だ。このうち20%はLPDDRの試作に充てられ、長江メモリ初のDRAM生産拠点となる。

サプライチェーン関係者によると、世界的にメモリーチップが不足しており、中国のメモリーチップメーカー2社が国内市場の自給率向上を担っている。両社は2027年末または2028年末までに、中国国内メモリーチップ市場の自給率を50%以上に引き上げることを目指している。

特に、中国政府が支援する重要プロジェクトや政府プロジェクトであるサーバー、およびByteDanceやTencentといった国有企業を背景とする他の民間クラウド企業に対しては、政策的な支援が提供される。中国国内市場は、高性能GPUや高帯域幅メモリ（HBM）の調達に課題を抱えているため、成熟したプロセス、コンピューティングクラスタの拡張、そして豊富なエネルギーを消費する並列アーキテクチャを通じて、AIコンピューティング能力の需要に対応していく。

注目すべきは、最近の市場の噂によると、長江メモリテクノロジーズ（YMTC）はNANDをサードパーティの独立系モジュールメーカーに販売し、それらのメーカーが顧客を通じてエンタープライズグレードのソリッドステートドライブ（SSD）に組み立てることで、原産地の機密性を回避しているという点である。さらに、北米の新規クラウドプロバイダーが試験生産を開始しており、2027年の武漢第3工場の生産能力拡張に伴い、海外供給比率を高める戦略は今後も拡大していくと予想される。

DDR5/LPDDR5の供給が逼迫する中、長新メモリも最近、米国とカナダの中小規模クラウドコンピューティング企業から認証を取得し、生産能力を事前に確保しようとしている。

北米のサーバー顧客は需要が最も大きく、支払意欲も最も高いため、中国製のメモリウェハーが海外で転売される際には、東南アジアのような小規模市場向けではなく、北米のクラウド顧客向けに「非公式な」ルートで優先的に供給される。

業界関係者が非公式に明らかにしたところによると、米国の民間企業は現在、「原則として」長江メモリテクノロジーズ（YMTC）または長新メモリテクノロジーズから製品を購入することが認められている。YMTCは商務省の「エンティティリスト」規制に基づき貿易ブラックリストに掲載されているが、その主な目的はYMTCが米国技術を購入または使用するための経路を遮断すること、そして米国の顧客が購入時にサプライチェーンのコンプライアンスリスクをより慎重に評価するように促すことにある。

しかし、一般的な民間調達は「完全に禁止されているわけではない」ため、ノートパソコンや消費者向けアプリケーションの調達は徐々に再開されている。ただし、調達範囲がクラウドデータセンターにまで拡大されると、より高度な機密性が求められる可能性がある。

一方、クラウドプロバイダーは、コンピューティング能力サービスのレンタルや運用業務のアウトソーシングといったモデルを採用し、第三者にデータセンター資産の所有と構築を委託することで、米国の大手企業が月額料金やサービス料を支払うだけで済むようにし、特定の物理コンポーネントを直接購入する際に生じる規制リスクを回避している。

アップルが最近、中国のメモリメーカーからの供給を拡大する意向を示したことで注目を集めているものの、サプライチェーン関係者は、アップルはAI時代においてその地位を失い、業界の需給への影響は大幅に低下したと考えている。

例えば、マイクロンは、アップルが中国のサプライチェーンにおける品質管理と量産安定性の向上を支援していることに不満を抱いている。中国企業にとって、アップルのサプライチェーンに参入することは、自社の品質が国際的な大手メーカーと同等のレベルに達したことの証明に過ぎず、大量供給や価格競争を行うつもりはないからだ。

業界関係者によると、近年、アップルの社内調達スタッフもNVIDIAに引き抜かれているという。アップルが長新や長村の生産能力に頼って調達コストを削減しようとするなら、2026年に望む結果が得られないだけでなく、2027年には生産能力がほとんど残っていないだろう。

アップルの調達が米中間の地政学的争いにおける政治的な駆け引きの材料となっているため、中国の二大メモリメーカーは、事業拡大を続けているにもかかわらず、短期的には中国市場におけるアップルのメモリ需要を満たすことは依然として困難だろう。

「どこまでがこちら側で、どこからが向こう側なのか」

content:
📘【半導体・MLCC・データセンター関連銘柄まとめ】8月25日

前夜のSOX指数▲2.7％で朝方は売りが先行したものの、日経平均の6万5,000円割れから押し目買いと先物のショートカバー。

イビデン、SUMCO、KOKUSAI ELECTRICなどが切り返す一方、アドバンテスト・ディスコは戻し切れず、NVIDIA決算前の選別が継続📈

🟢 イビデン：+6.3％
🟢 SUMCO：+2.7％
🟢 KOKUSAI ELECTRIC：+2.5％
🟢 ソフトバンクグループ：+2.3％
🟢 太陽誘電：+1.3％
🟢 SCREEN HD：+1.2％
🟢 村田製作所：+0.9％
🟢 キオクシアHD：+0.7％
🟢 東京エレクトロン：+0.5％
🟢 レーザーテック：+0.4％
🟥 アドバンテスト：▲0.1％
🟥 信越化学工業：▲0.8％
🟥 ルネサスエレクトロニクス：▲0.8％
🟥 ディスコ：▲1.2％

本日の背景は、

・前夜の米SOX指数が▲2.7％
・NVIDIA決算前の持ち高調整
・米AI・メモリー株安
・中国NAND企業の増産・競争激化への警戒
・朝方の韓国半導体株安
・日経平均が一時918円安
・6万5,000円割れで押し目買い
・KOSPIの下げ渋り
・米株先物上昇
・日米金利と原油の落ち着き
・先物と高ベータ株のショートカバー

です。

本日の流れは、

米半導体株安
↓
朝方はAI・半導体株を中心にデリスキング
↓
日経平均が6万5,000円を割り込む
↓
押し目買いと先物のショートカバー
↓
ICパッケージ基板・ウェハー・成膜装置・MLCCが反発
↓
NVIDIA決算との連動性が高いテスター・加工装置は戻り限定

となりました。

銘柄別では、

🟢 イビデン：+6.3％

AIサーバー向け高性能ICパッケージ基板の代表銘柄として大幅高。

新たな個別材料より、朝方の売り一巡後に先端パッケージ需要への期待とショートカバーが集中しました。

本日の半導体関連で最も強く、AIインフラ投資の中でもGPU周辺のボトルネック銘柄が選ばれた動きです。

🟢 SUMCO：+2.7％

シリコンウェハー株に買い戻し。

ウェハー需要が急改善したことを示す新たな材料というより、前週までの調整と売られ過ぎを意識した自律反発が中心です。

半導体高ベータ株より出遅れていた素材株への資金移動も追い風となりました。

🟢 KOKUSAI ELECTRIC：+2.5％

成膜・熱処理装置株として反発。

HBM向けDRAMや先端ロジックの多層化・微細化に伴う装置需要への期待から、朝方の売り一巡後に押し目買いが入りました。

ただし、NVIDIA決算前で上値追いは慎重です。

🟢 ソフトバンクグループ：+2.3％

朝方はAI・半導体株安の影響を受けましたが、日経平均先物の切り返しとともに反発。

ArmやAIインフラ投資への期待を持つ高ベータ株として、ショートカバーの影響も受けました。

本日の上昇は、新規材料より指数・需給主導の側面が強い動きです。

🟢 太陽誘電：+1.3％

前週の大株主売却を受けた需給悪化から、自律反発が継続。

AIサーバー、自動車、産業機器向けの高容量MLCC需要への期待も下支えしました。

ただし、大株主売却に伴う需給整理が完全に終わったかは引き続き確認が必要です。

🟢 SCREEN HD：+1.2％

半導体洗浄装置株として押し目買い。

前夜の米半導体株安にもかかわらずプラスを確保しており、半導体需要全面悪化ではないことを示す動きです。

東京エレクトロンやレーザーテックより上昇率が高く、製造装置株内でも選別がみられました。

🟢 村田製作所：+0.9％

太陽誘電とともにMLCC関連が反発。

AIサーバーや自動車の電子化に伴う中長期需要への期待が残る中、前週の大幅調整から押し目買いが入りました。

テーマ全体の買い戻しが中心で、新たな個別材料より需給主導です。

🟢 キオクシアHD：+0.7％

前日の🟥 ▲6.2％から小幅反発。

朝方は米メモリー株安や中国NAND企業の増産・競争激化への警戒で売られましたが、KOSPIの下げ渋りと日経平均の切り返しを受けてプラスへ回復しました。

ただし、NAND需給への警戒が残り、戻りは限定的でした。

🟢 東京エレクトロン：+0.5％

朝方の売りから切り返して小幅高。

中長期のAI半導体設備投資期待は残るものの、NVIDIA決算前で積極的な上値追いは限定的でした。

KOKUSAI ELECTRICやSCREEN HDより戻りが弱く、製造装置株が一様に買われたわけではありません。

🟢 レーザーテック：+0.4％

先端半導体投資の代表的な高PER銘柄として、朝方は金利・米半導体株安の影響を受けました。

その後は押し目買いでプラスへ戻しましたが、NVIDIA決算前の持ち高調整が残り、上昇率は小幅にとどまりました。

🟥 アドバンテスト：▲0.1％

NVIDIAやAIアクセラレーター向けテスター需要との連動性が高く、決算前の警戒が最も残りやすい銘柄。

日経平均は大きく切り返しましたが、終値ではマイナス圏を脱し切れませんでした。

AI需要悪化というより、イベント前のポジション調整が重荷です。

🟥 信越化学工業：▲0.8％

半導体用シリコンウェハー・材料株として軟調。

SUMCOには買い戻しが入った一方、信越化学工業には資金が広がらず、素材株内でも強弱が分かれました。

新たな個別悪材料より、需要回復時期への慎重姿勢と大型株の持ち高調整が中心です。

🟥 ルネサスエレクトロニクス：▲0.8％

自動車・産業機器向け半導体が中心で、NVIDIA決算との直接的な連動性は比較的限定的。

それでも朝方の半導体バスケット売りに押され、後場の買い戻しでもプラス圏へ戻せませんでした。

AI関連の反発が自動車・産業向け半導体まで広がらなかった動きです。

🟥 ディスコ：▲1.2％

HBM・先端ロジック向けの切断、研削、薄化需要への中長期期待は残っています。

一方、高PER・高ベータの加工装置株として、NVIDIA決算前の利益確定と持ち高整理が継続。

半導体テーマがプラスへ切り返す中でも戻り切れず、本日の関連銘柄では最も弱い動きとなりました。

つまり本日は、

ICパッケージ基板
→ イビデンが大幅高

ウェハー・材料
→ SUMCOは反発、信越化学は弱い

成膜・洗浄装置
→ KOKUSAI ELECTRIC、SCREEN HDが上昇

MLCC
→ 太陽誘電、村田製作所が反発

メモリー
→ キオクシアHDは小幅高へ回復

テスター・加工装置
→ アドバンテスト、ディスコは戻り限定

AIインフラ大型株
→ ソフトバンクグループがショートカバーで上昇

という構造でした。

重要なのは、

「AI・半導体需要への懸念が解消した」

のではなく、

「朝方の売りが買い戻された後、NVIDIA決算との距離や需給、バリュエーションを基準に資金の強弱が分かれた」

という点です。

今後は、

title: UN announces new initiative to protect terrorism victims from online harm and re-traumatization
content: The United Nations on Friday launched a new initiative to safeguard victims of terror attacks from online harm and re-traumatization, with its primary aim being to ensure a victim-centered approach to building a safer environment for internet users. Friday, i.e, August 21, marks the International Day of Remembrance of and Tribute to the Victims of Terrorism. First established in 2017 through Resolution 72/165 , August 21 is commemorated to honour and support terror attack victims and survivors and promote and protect human rights and freedoms. Last year, the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT) launched the Victims of Terrorism Associations Network (VoTAN). One of the key outcomes of the first UN Global Congress of Victims of Terrorism held in 2022 was to bring victims, survivors, victims’ associations and other civil society organizations together and provide a safe space to support each other and engage in advocacy to bring about meaningful change. Presently, VoTAN connects 120 victims and victims’ associations across 40 countries. This year, VoTAN released a briefing paper, entitled “Building a Safer Internet for Victims of Terrorism.” In commenting on the importance of the briefing paper and calling for better safeguards to be put into place to further protect vulnerable people, Alexandre Zouev, Acting Under-Secretary-General for Counter Terrorism, UNOCT stated: Drawing directly on lived experiences of victims and survivors, it offers recommendations to governments, technology companies, and civil societies to help create digital spaces that protect rather than re-traumatise those affected by terrorism. The event further followed up with experiences being shared by survivors of several devastating terror attacks across the globe. While introducing the briefing paper, Dr Maysoon Salama, Manager of An-Nur Child Care Centre, explained how platforms often trigger trauma long after the crises fade. title: UN warns humanitarian aid cuts leave children vulnerable to hunger in Somalia
content: The UN warned on Friday that the global decrease in funding for humanitarian aid has forced aid programs and facilities in Somalia to shut down, and is resulting in increasingly severe consequences for Somali children. According to UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) spokesperson James Elder, aid cuts closed doors to healthcare and deprived people, including children, of access to water and education. The UN reported that the unprecedented cuts in humanitarian aid have led over 200 health and nutrition facilities to close in Somalia, which has contributed to a 32 percent increase in Somali children admitted to stabilization centers with severe acute malnutrition . The UN stressed that the reason behind this increase is not due to the fact that more children are getting sick but rather to the loss of access to preventive and community-based nutrition services. Furthermore, the UN highlighted that these funding cuts come at a critical time for Somalia, where humanitarian needs continue to escalate due to ongoing armed conflict and the impacts of El Ni ñ o . Based on UN projections, nearly 1.9 million children in Somalia are expected to be affected by malnutrition, with almost half a million expected to experience the severe acute form, amid persistent armed conflict, displacement, and extreme food insecurity in the region. On the other hand, Somalia is also undergoing severe droughts in the north, while also preparing for extreme flooding caused by El Niño weather pattern, which will further hinder agriculture and food access. Nevertheless, the UN stressed that its aid programs can improve the humanitarian situation in Somalia only if adequate funding is available, emphasizing that the agency would not be able to keep up its humanitarian response under current financial constraints. title: US deports over 160 people to Haiti following end of protected status
content: ICE deported over 160 individuals to Haiti on Thursday in the wake of the US Supreme Court’s decision to uphold the administrative repeal of temporary protected status (TPS) for roughly 330,000 Haitians, despite pervasive gang violence throughout the country. The charter flight landed in the northern city of Cap-Haïtien, instead of capital Port-au-Prince, as gangs reportedly control roughly 70 percent of the capital city and surrounding areas. Officials reportedly feared arriving deportees would quickly become gang targets. According to the d irector general of Haiti’s National Office of Migration, Jean Négot Bonheur Delva, among the deportees were former TPS holders, as well as individuals who previously served prison sentences, and even people of Haitian decent but born elsewhere. Multiple humanitarian groups have called for deportations to Haiti to halt immediately, arguing that the nation is too dangerous, particularly for women and children. The US State Department continues to list Haiti as a “ Do not travel ” country in its Travel Advisory report. The deportation marks the first act of removal to Haiti following President Donald Trump’s revocation of TPS for Haitian immigrants. The program had previously allowed individuals to live and work in the US for 18 month increments as a way to seek protection from violence and social upheaval within Haiti. In June, the Supreme Court upheld the administrative decision to end the program, reasoning that the decision came under sole executive discretion. Dissenting justices argued that under closer examination, certain Trump statements about Haitian migrants revealed racially charged motivations for ending the program, which allow the court to more closely scrutinize the executive action. The ruling overturned a federal appellate court decision in January that struck down the administrative action on grounds that then-Homeland Security director Kristi Noem had exceeded congressionally authorized
author: Max Robinette | U. Pittsburgh School of Law, US

title: Federal judge strikes down administration’s ban on visas for immigrants from 75 countries
content: A judge for the US District Court for the Southern District of New York on Friday struck down a ban on immigrant visas for citizens of 75 countries. Judge Jeannette Vargas wrote that the order, from Secretary of State Marco Rubio, was “patently unlawful” and exceeded his power under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) , which “explicitly strips the Secretary of State of authority over consular adjudication of immigrant visas.” Rubio issued the order to consular officers in January. He directed them to deny immigrant visas to residents of the 75 countries, primarily in Latin America, Africa, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and the Caribbean. The order affected about 40% of the world’s nations. The public charge rule is the stated basis of the order. Prospective immigrants must show that they will not become public charges, or persons who depend on the government for subsistence. In July, the Trump Administration announced that it would deny green cards to immigrants who use any public assistance, based on the rule. Catholic Legal Immigration Network and African Communities Together sued to block the order. The INA requires consular officers to conduct individualized assessments of applicants, considering such factors as job skills, savings, and support from friends or family who are already in the US. Vargas wrote: The Policy, which categorically prohibits the issuance of immigrant visas based upon the nationality of the applicant, represents a direct abrogation of this statutory scheme. [Rubio’s order] mandates the refusal of visas to eligible applicants without any basis in law… [W]hatever determinations [consular officers] make as to eligibility for the applicants…are ultimately irrelevant. The outcome is predetermined. The visa will be refused. title: Human Rights Watch expresses alarm over escalating settler violence on West Bank
content: Human Rights Watch (HRW) warned on Thursday that escalating settler violence and aggressive settler expansion in the occupied West Bank is driving the displacement of Palestinians, with the organization attributing the rise of settler extremism to Israeli authorities. HRW conducted investigations over April and May 2026 within 7 Palestinian West Bank communities. The organization expressed alarm over the spike of killings between March and April 2026, “including of children.” HRW said there was also a spike in “assaults, sexual violence, physical and mental abuse, arbitrary detention, arson, property destruction, and theft.” HRW reported the complicity of the military, stating that armed settlers “at times, [acted] alongside Israeli army units,” and that soldiers were present during instances of settler violence, but failed to intervene. The armed settlers, according to sources interviewed by HRW, are destroying livestock and crops, “restricting access to water and grazing land”, and attacking Palestinian “residents and property.” In June, the UN highlighted alarming attacks against Palestinian children by Israeli settlers, and threats of sexual violence against Palestinian women and girls. Sarah Sanbar, HRW Acting Israel and Palestine researcher, attributed the enabling of settler violence and extremism to the Israeli authorities. Sanbar said that the authorities provide weapons, “legal cover,” and funding. She stated: The Israeli government and the settlers share the same goal of maximum land and minimum Palestinians, with the authorities not only failing to stop settler violence, but actively enabling it. In June, Amnesty International released an executive summary on the ethnic cleansing of Palestinians by the settlers supported by the Israeli military. title: UN warns that civilians in Gaza face severe shelter crisis as strikes and gunfire continue
content: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Thursday that 2.1 million Palestinian civilians are in need of shelter, essential household items, and protection from airstrikes and gunfire. OCHA reported that Palestinian civilians are being “killed, injured or otherwise affected by air strikes, shelling and gunfire.” On Wednesday, a 13-year-old girl was among those killed. OCHA highlighted that the shelter severity situation is making it extremely unsafe for civilians and contributing to the wider humanitarian crisis. The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), in partnership with OCHA, published a report on the shelter crisis in Gaza on Thursday. The report revealed that 94 percent of households in Gaza require basic household necessities and essentials, such as fuel, energy, and water. According to the report, an estimated 1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza do not have adequate shelter. Commenting on the severity of the situation facing Palestinians on the ground, Shelter Cluster coordinator Jehan Salim stated: A shelter is not adequate simply because it has four walls or a roof. Families need to be able to sleep, cook, wash and keep their children safe inside it. Ten months after the ceasefire , most families have lived more than a year in shelters that were never designed for long-term accommodation. Salim also warned that essential materials to help build adequate shelters and repair and restore homes are currently unable to enter Gaza in the quantities and scale required. According to the NRC report, restrictions on these materials and inadequate funding has “kept assistance far below the level of need.” According to OCHA, an estimated USD$562 million in funding is needed to address the shelter crisis. title: Amnesty International calls upon Hamas to ‘stamp out’ extrajudicial executions and ensure justice for victims in the Gaza Strip
content: Amnesty International on Friday issued a call for authorities and forces affiliated with Hamas in the occupied Gaza Strip to put an end to extrajudicial executions of suspected collaborators with Israel. In recent months, security officials in Hamas’ military wing —the Al-Qassam Brigades—publicly announced the summary execution of one man for collaborating with Israel and their intention to execute another “informant” within days as part of a broader “large-scale security” campaign. While Hamas officials assert that they have opened preliminary investigations into the incidents, none of those responsible for the killings have been held to account to date, Amnesty International reports. A report published in June by the UN identified 249 cases of extrajudicial executions and severe physical violence in Gaza between August 2024 and early 2026, at least 60 of which involved Hamas-affiliated forces. Amnesty International has also investigated and documented an additional nine extrajudicial executions and other unlawful killings by Hamas-affiliated forces, committed in the immediate aftermath of the October 2025 ceasefire between Israel and Hamas. Taken together, Amnesty says, the cases point to a broader pattern of unlawful killings carried out with little prospect of accountability—a trend the organization says must end immediately. “Nearly three years into Israel’s ongoing genocide against Palestinians in the occupied Gaza Strip, the traumatized civilian population has already endured unimaginable suffering and cannot be subjected to further killings, abuses, and cruelty,” said Erika Guevara-Rosas, s enior director for research and advocacy at Amnesty International. “The Hamas authorities must immediately halt all unlawful killings, acts of vigilantism and arbitrary arrests.” She continued: “Restoring law and order must never serve as a cover to commit grave human rights violations, carry out reprisals, or to collectively punish entire families.” Hamas officials have

title: Rights group sues Canada and Manitoba for ‘extremely underfunded’ legal aid
content: The Canadian Civil Liberties Association on Thursday sued the governments of Canada and Manitoba for the province’s “extremely underfunded” criminal legal aid, arguing that the underfunding violates the right to a fair trial and the presumption of innocence, and is discriminatory against Indigenous people in effect. The lawsuit argued that the financial eligibility criteria for criminal legal aid was unduly restrictive. It explained that the current annual gross income threshold does not factor in rising legal costs and living expenses in the province. It also challenged the aid’s narrow scope of compulsory coverage to only indictable offenses under the provincial Legal Aid Regulations . Yet, summary convictions can still result in imprisonment of two years less a day. The group argued that the limited coverage deprives defendants of their ability to mount a complete defense. Even with an approved legal aid, the amount is insufficient for defendants to retain effective representation in a criminal case, the group asserted. It observed that Manitoba’s criminal legal aid, with the lowest spend per case across Canada, incentivized premature guilty pleas. The lawsuit included a 2021 study , conducted within Ontario. It revealed the common phenomenon of defendants entering false guilty pleas because they had no other realistic alternatives due to a basket of factors, including inadequate legal aid, lengthy pre-trial custody and routine bail denials. The group also highlighted the disproportionate impact on Indigenous defendants of the underfunding. This is premised on the higher rate of economic disadvantages and overrepresentation in the criminal justice system–effects of widespread systemic discrimination against the Indigenous community. Howard Sapers, executive director of the association, reiterated that government policies cannot deny Charter rights. title: プラネックスの2.5Gbpsスイッチングハブ、放熱対策とか大丈夫？ 元・中の人が裏技3選を伝授します【奥川浩彦の「岐阜の山奥に移住しました」第13回】
content: 前回は移住先の有線LAN環境についてお伝えした。筆者は速さと安定性でデスクトップPC、NAS、レコーダー、TVなどを、できるだけ有線LANで接続したいと思っている。その中でも仕事関連のPCやNASは2.5Gbps化を進めている。連載の第13回となる今回は、Synology NASの2.5Gbps化、2.5Gbpsスイッチングハブの裏技など、移住とは話がズレるが、INTERNET Watch読者の参考になるかもしれない話を30枚ほどの画像を用いてお伝えしよう。
author: 奥川浩彦@ アイピーアール
